claim: Concurrent submissions can receive the same next version number because version allocation and insertion are separate operations.
trigger: Two requests for the same artifact pass authentication and call submit_version concurrently after observing the same current index; both next_version calls return N before either add_version updates the index.
impact: Both uploads use artifact-{id}-vN; the later index update replaces the earlier version entry and deletes the earlier Storage file, so one accepted submission is lost (and its canonical copy may remain orphaned).

evidence.detail: src/main.py:2611-2622 calls next_version then add_version without a per-artifact reservation/lock.
src/store.py:617-623 computes max(numbers)+1; src/store.py:537-552 uploads and only then mutates the index.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-artifact-hub-design.md:109-113 requires each version to be its own Storage file and numbers count up.

suggested_fix: Atomically reserve the next version per artifact (and coordinate across replicas) before upload, or use a conflict-safe Storage allocation scheme.

def _resolve(self, artifact_id: str) -> _ArtEntry | None:
        """Index lookup with a Storage fallback for artifacts we never saw.

        Another replica may have written after our last hydrate, so an index
        miss is re-checked against Storage before we answer "not found".
        """
        with self._lock:
            entry = self._index.get(artifact_id)
        if entry is not None:
            return entry

        files = self._backend.search_by_tag(tag_for_id(artifact_id))
        if not files:
            return None
        fresh = _ArtEntry()
        for info in files:
            _absorb_file(fresh, info)

        with self._lock:
            current = self._index.get(artifact_id)
            if current is None:
                self._index[artifact_id] = fresh
                return fresh
            return current
claim: An existing in-memory artifact index is never refreshed from Storage, so replicas can serve permanently stale version and metadata state after another replica writes.
trigger: Replica A hydrates artifact X with v1, then replica B uploads v2 or changes metadata; a request handled by A calls _resolve(X), finds its existing entry, and returns it without search_by_tag or merge.
impact: Replica A can continue serving an old head, omit a newly submitted version, or authorize/validate mutations against stale owner/settings until restart or another local update; the documented multi-replica fallback only handles index misses.

evidence.detail: src/store.py:457-463 explicitly returns an existing entry before querying Storage; only the miss path at 465-477 searches and installs fresh state.
src/main.py:260-263 hydrates once at startup; no periodic or per-request refresh is present.

_review/codemap.md deployment assumptions mark replica count UNKNOWN and identify startup hydration/in-memory index; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-artifact-hub-design.md:79 describes startup hydration and disk LRU.

suggested_fix: Use a shared/versioned state source or refresh existing entries with a bounded consistency strategy before serving and mutating.

def delete(self, artifact_id: str) -> bool:
        """Delete every Storage file of an artifact and purge the caches."""
        files: list[FileInfo] = self._backend.search_by_tag(tag_for_id(artifact_id))
        deleted = False
        for info in files:
            try:
                self._backend.delete(info.id)
                deleted = True
            except BackendError as exc:
                logger.warning(
                    "Cannot delete file %s of artifact %s: %s",
                    info.id,
                    artifact_id,
                    exc,
                )

        with self._lock:
            self._index.pop(artifact_id, None)
            self._forget_memory_locked(artifact_id)
            self._forget_meta_locked(artifact_id)
        self._purge_disk_cache(artifact_id)
        return deleted
claim: Artifact deletion is a non-atomic list-then-delete sequence, allowing a concurrent version/meta upload to survive deletion while the local index is purged.
trigger: A DELETE request completes search_by_tag, then another request uploads a version or meta file before the delete loop/index purge finishes; the new file is not in the captured list and is left in Storage, while the deleting process removes its index entry.
impact: The API reports deletion even though newly written serving data remains in Storage; the same process returns not-found until a later hydration or miss-based rebuild, and a later replica may rediscover the supposedly deleted artifact.

evidence.detail: src/store.py:692 obtains one snapshot list, then deletes only those IDs at 694-704; index/cache purge occurs afterward at 706-710.
src/main.py:2488-2503 exposes this through the authenticated DELETE /api/artifacts/{id} route, while update/submission paths can write versions concurrently.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-artifact-hub-design.md:68 promises DELETE /api/artifacts/{id} deletes the serving copy; lines 109-120 define separate version/meta files.

suggested_fix: Coordinate deletion with writes using a per-artifact/shared lock or deletion tombstone and recheck until no newer files can be committed.
